record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For magnetic Schrödinger operators, determine whether the optimal magnetic Lieb-Thirring constant L^mag_{γ,d} in sum_n |E_n((−i∇+A)^2+V)|^γ ≤ L^mag_{γ,d} ∫_{R^d} V_-(x)^(γ+d/2) dx always coincides with the non-magnetic optimal constant L_{γ,d}.

evidence.quote: It is an open problem, however, whether the optimal constant Lmagγ,d coincides with the optimal constant Lγ,d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 1$ and $\gamma\geq 0$. For a magnetic vector potential $A:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ (sufficiently regular) and a real-valued potential $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ with $V_-:=\max(-V,0)\in L^{\gamma+d/2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, consider the magnetic Schrödinger operator
$$H_{A,V}=(-i\nabla+A)^2+V$$
acting in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, and let $\{E_n(H_{A,V})\}$ denote its negative eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity).

Define the optimal magnetic Lieb–Thirring constant $L^{\mathrm{mag}}_{\gamma,d}$ as the smallest constant such that
$$\sum_n |E_n(H_{A,V})|^{\gamma} \;\leq\; L^{\mathrm{mag}}_{\gamma,d}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma+d/2}\,dx$$
holds for all admissible $A$ and $V$. Define the optimal non-magnetic Lieb–Thirring constant $L_{\gamma,d}$ analogously, but only for $A\equiv 0$.

It is known that $L_{\gamma,d}\leq L^{\mathrm{mag}}_{\gamma,d}$. Determine, for each pair $(\gamma,d)$ with $\gamma\geq 0$ and $d\geq 1$ (within the regime where the inequality is meaningful, i.e., $\gamma\geq 1/2$ if $d=1$ and $\gamma>0$ if $d=2$, $\gamma\geq 0$ if $d\geq 3$), whether the equality
$$L^{\mathrm{mag}}_{\gamma,d}=L_{\gamma,d}$$
holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The question whether the optimal magnetic Lieb–Thirring constant equals the non-magnetic one appears to remain open. While all currently known explicit upper bounds for the non-magnetic constants extend without change to the magnetic case, no general proof of equality (nor a counterexample) is known.

status_evidence.title: Lieb–Thirring inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Although all presently known constants remain unchanged, it is not known whether this is true in general for the best possible constant.
status_evidence.claim: Whether the optimal magnetic and non-magnetic Lieb–Thirring constants coincide is not known.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic Lieb-Thirring inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Magnetic Lieb-Thirring inequalities establish bounds for sums of negative eigenvalues of magnetic Schrödinger operators.
status_evidence.claim: Magnetic Lieb-Thirring inequalities are known but optimal constants in the magnetic case are not established to equal the non-magnetic ones.
